unitTitle: I'd Like a Plate of Noodles
title: Speaking & Writing
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah mempelajari kosakata tambahan tentang rasa makanan dan minuman serta memahami teks tentang memilih menu di restoran.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 70-71
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will be able to ask and answer questions about their likes and dislikes for foods and drinks, and explain why.
Learners will be able to describe food and drinks using adverbs (too, a little, very, really) with taste words.
Learners will learn to be respectful and show good behaviour when eating at a restaurant.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
Ask a quick food question to set the mood, e.g. “What did you have for breakfast this morning?”
Play the letter game with a food twist. The teacher writes his/her name on the board and says a food or drink that starts with the same letter (e.g. Susan – soup).
Ask the students whose names start with that letter to stand up, say their name and a food or drink starting with the same letter (e.g. Nina – noodles). Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives: hot potato and throw the ball, where the student holding the ball says one food or drink in English.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 70.

First, the teacher reads the questions in the speech bubble at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear, e.g. “Do you like your bowl of fried rice?” – “Yes, it’s really tasty.” / “No, it’s too salty.”
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the questions in the speech bubble aloud as a class.
Then, ask students to ask and answer the questions, in pairs.
Model to the students how the questions can be changed by changing some of the key vocabulary (e.g. “Do you like your glass of lemon iced tea?” – “No, it’s too sour.”).

Now, put them in different pairs and ask them to substitute some of the key vocabulary in the questions so they can practice asking about different things. This can be repeated several times by putting students into different pairs.

Explain the adverbs in the Language Box: ‘a little’, ‘very’, ‘really’ and ‘too’. Point out that ‘too’ is only for a negative meaning (“It is too tasty.” → “It is really tasty.”) and that the adverb comes before the adjective (“It is sweet a little.” → “It is a little sweet.”).
Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes). This can be used to help answer students' questions.
Ask students to look at Speaking and Writing B on Student Book page 70 and ask some instruction-checking questions, e.g. Which activity are we doing? What page is it on? What do you have to do?
Put students in groups of four. Tell them that they will take turns acting as the waiter for the other three group members.
The waiter asks each customer the four questions in the Q&A speech bubbles (food order, drink order, and whether they like their food and drink) and writes down the four answers for each person.

Read number one together as a class as the example, e.g. Name: Gina – Food order: a bowl of fried rice – Drink order: a glass of lemon iced tea – “Yes, this bowl of fried rice is really tasty.” – “No, this glass of lemon iced tea is too sour.”
Give students around 12-15 minutes and monitor the groups to help them if needed.
Elicit answers from the groups. Answers will vary, but they should follow the sentence pattern shown in the Language Box on this page.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Put students in new groups of four.
Repeat the waiter activity. Tell students they have to order different food and drinks and give different answers this time (e.g. “No, these pieces of fried chicken are too spicy.”).
Ask students to write their group members’ answers in their notebooks.
Ask some students to read one or two of their sentences aloud to the class, paying attention to ‘this’ for one item and ‘these’ for plural items.
Direct the students to look at the picture on page 71 and ask them “What can you see on the page?” to elicit some answers.

Next, tell students to read the text about the Teen Value (Social & Interpersonal Skills: demonstrating good behaviour in public places). They can read it silently, or put them in pairs to share reading the text aloud together, sentence by sentence.
Elicit from students, “What is the key focus of this Teen Corner page?”, and “Why do you think being respectful at a restaurant is important?”
Ask students to look at activity A and read the instructions as given on the page. Ask some instruction-checking questions to check if students understand the task.
Put students in groups of three or four students.
Tell them to practice acting out the respectful scenario. Give them about 5-7 minutes to practice.
Then, ask each group to act out the scenario for the class.
Ask students to look at activity B and read the instructions as given on the page.
Keep students in their groups of three or four and tell them that they have about 8-10 minutes to write their own short roleplay about respectful behaviour at a restaurant.

Show the sample roleplay as an example, e.g. Student 1: “Good afternoon. We would like two burgers and two bowls of soup, please.” Student 2: “And four glasses of water, thank you.” Student 3: (puts phone away) “Let’s talk while we wait.” Waiter: “Thank you. Your food will be ready soon.”
While students are writing their roleplays, monitor the class and be available to give help and suggestions as needed.
Ask students to look at activity C and read the instructions as given on the page.
Tell the groups to practice acting out their roleplay for around 5-7 minutes.
Then, ask each group to act out their roleplay for the class.

Give positive feedback, and after each roleplay ask the class, “Was the role play showing respectful behavior? How do you feel when people show respectful behaviour?” Elicit responses from a few students (e.g. “I feel happy and comfortable when people speak politely.”).
Ask students to look at activity D and read the instructions as given on the page.

Put students in pairs and tell them to write a list of four actions that are respectful at a restaurant and four actions that are disrespectful (e.g. say “please” and “thank you” to the staff, put your phone away during the meal / talk too loudly, make a mess).
Then, put two pairs of students together and ask them to share their lists with each other.
Wrap up the class by highlighting that showing respectful behaviour in public places, like a restaurant, makes everyone feel comfortable and shows kindness to the staff and other customers.
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: unjuk kerja speaking berpasangan (kelancaran, ketepatan, keberanian).
Produk tulisan sederhana sesuai model di Student Book (struktur & kosakata unit).
Umpan balik teman sebaya dan guru terhadap hasil speaking/writing.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
